info.title: AEM Admin API Service
info.description: AEM Admin API Service is used to manage the lifecycle of content, code, and configuration.

tags.name: authentication
tags.description:
The API uses your existing Identity Provider (IDP) to authenticate users with administrative access. The general flow is that you open `/login` in a browser, select the IDP you want to use, and then are redirected to the IDP login page. After successful login, you are redirected back to the Admin API with an auth token in the response cookie (`auth_token`). This token is then used to authenticate all subsequent requests.

Alternatively, you can provide an `authorization: token $API_KEY` header. In order to obtain an API_KEY, use the Site Config Property API to create one.

post.description:
A bulk publish is started if the request body contains a `paths` property. It must be a non-empty array, and the request must target the live root (`/live/`). Publishing of subtrees (paths ending with `/*`) is not supported.
By default, only new and modified resources are updated, unless the `forceUpdate` property is set to `true`.
If the `delete` property is set to `true`, the specified resources are unpublished instead.
The bulk job is executed synchronously and the response contains the completed job. If more than 200 paths are specified, `forceAsync` must be set to `true`, in which case the job is executed asynchronously and this request returns information about the created job.

get.description: Returns logs for a project. If there are more logs for the timespan specified, there will be a `next` link in the response to load the next batch. Pagination tokens identify a journal range and can be used without time parameters. Token-only responses omit `from` and `to`. Each page contains at most 1000 entries, with a target maximum size of 3 MB of serialized entries (at least one entry is returned).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries per page. Invalid values use the default.

success.description: Success response of a log request.

post.description:
A bulk preview is started if the request body contains a `paths` property. It must be a non-empty array, and the request must target the preview root (`/preview/`). If a path ends with `/*`, it is assumed to be a folder and is recursively previewed.
By default, only new and modified resources are updated, unless the `forceUpdate` property is set to `true`.
If the `delete` property is set to `true`, the specified resources are removed from preview instead.
The bulk job is executed synchronously and the response contains the completed job. If the number of paths exceeds the synchronous limit of the content source, `forceAsync` must be set to `true`, in which case the job is executed asynchronously and this request returns information about the created job.

post.description:
Creates a document in the source bus. External images are interned in the media bus and
references to these images are updated. The document is also pretty-printed.

requestBody.description:
The raw content of the document to create, its
format must be indicated by the `Content-Type` request header (e.g.
`text/html` for documents, `application/json`,
`application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, etc.).

etag.description: ETag returned by storage for the written document, in the same format as GET and HEAD.

put.description:
Creates or replaces a document in the content bus. The document is assumed to not have external images. If external images are present, they are rejected with a 400 error. In that case the document should be created using the POST method instead to have those images interned.
When the `source` query parameter is provided, copies the document from the `source` path to the specified path. The `collision` parameter controls behavior when the destination already exists.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Source path for copy operations. When provided, the document at this path is copied to the destination path. The value is specified rooted as an absolute path from the site root.

parameters.name: collision
parameters.description: Collision handling strategy when the destination already exists. Set to `overwrite` to replace the existing resource. Set to `unique` to append a (base-36) encoded timestamp to the destination name to make it unique. These timestamps are alphabetically sortable.

requestBody.description:
The raw content of the document to create. Only required when the
`source` query parameter is not provided; for copy operations the
body is omitted and the destination is populated from `source` instead.
When a body is provided, its format must be indicated by the
`Content-Type` request header (e.g. `text/html` for documents,
`application/json`, `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, etc.).

schema.description:
Result of the copy, containing the list of source/destination
path pairs.

etag.description: ETag returned by storage for the written document, in the same format as GET and HEAD.

409.description:
Conflict. Typically returned when a document already exists at the
destination path. Set the `collision` query parameter to resolve it:
use `overwrite` to replace the existing document, or `unique` to have
the destination name made unique. The `x-error` response
header provides details about the specific problem.

delete.description:
Deletes a document by moving it to the .trash folder.
Before it's moved, a version is created for the document in the version store.
If the document is already in the .trash folder, it is just deleted from there. The version store of the document is left in place, so documents can always be restored from there.

get.description:
Lists the contents of a folder (path ending with `/`).
Returns an array of files and subfolders sorted by name. Underscores are accepted as name separators in folder names (for example, `en_us/`) and are not rewritten to hyphens. All other folder-name validation still applies.

post.description: Creates a folder in the content source (path ending with `/`) by placing a marker file in the folder. If the folder already exists, this operation has no effect.

put.description:
Copies a folder (path ending with `/`) and all of its contents recursively from the location given by the `source` query parameter to the specified path. The `collision` parameter controls behaviour when the destination already exists.
The `source` query parameter is required and must itself reference a folder (path ending with `/`); copying a file onto a folder path (or vice versa) is rejected with a 400.
No request body is accepted on this operation.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Source folder path (must end with `/`) to copy from. Specified as an absolute path from the site root.

parameters.name: collision
parameters.description: Collision handling strategy when the destination already exists. Set to `overwrite` to replace existing resources. Set to `unique` to append a (base-36) encoded timestamp to colliding destination names to make them unique. These timestamps are alphabetically sortable.

200.description: Folder copied. The response lists every file that was processed.

schema.description:
Result of the recursive copy, containing the list of
source/destination path pairs for every file in the folder
tree.

409.description:
Conflict. Typically returned when a file already exists at one of
the destination paths. Set the `collision` query parameter to
resolve it: use `overwrite` to replace the existing files, or
`unique` to have colliding destination names suffixed with a
sortable timestamp so the operation succeeds without overwriting.
The `x-error` response header provides details about the specific
problem.

delete.description:
Deletes a folder and all its contents recursively (a folder is a path ending with `/`). All the contents of the folder and subfolders are moved to the .trash folder.
Before they are moved, a new version of all the files is created.
If the folder is already in the .trash folder, it is just deleted from there. The versions of the documents are left in the version store and can be used for restore in case of accidental deletion.

post.description:
Creates a new version of a document. The version is created by copying the document to the version storage.
Optional query parameters `operation` and `comment` can be provided to annotate the version. An optional `If-Match` header pins the copy to the source document ETag returned by GET or HEAD. The precondition is enforced atomically when copying the source, not just before the copy. If the source has changed, the request fails with 412 without creating a version or retrying against newer content. Without `If-Match`, existing retry behavior is preserved.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: A single strong ETag from GET or HEAD of the source document, including its double quotes. This identifies the source document content, not the version collection. Empty values, weak ETags, lists of ETags, and `*` are not supported and return 400.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Operation that triggered the version creation (e.g. `preview`, `version`).

400.description: Invalid request or unsupported If-Match header.

412.description: The source document ETag did not match at copy time. No version was created.

get.description:
Lists all versions of a document, ordered from oldest to newest.
To retrieve a specific version, append the version id to the path: `/{org}/sites/{site}/source/{path}/.versions/{versionId}`.

Retrieves the content of a specific version of a document. The body is
returned as-is and its format is indicated by the `Content-Type` response
header (the same format the document had when the version was created).

parameters.name: versionId
parameters.description: Version identifier returned from the version listing.

200.description:
The raw content of the requested version. The body is returned as-is;
its format is indicated by the `Content-Type` response header.

content-type.description: Content type of the versioned document

content-length.description: Size of the versioned document in bytes

disableNotificationsParam.description: When set to `true`, suppresses change notifications for affected resources.

limitParam.name: limit
limitParam.description: Maximum number of entries to return. Defaults to 100 and is clamped between 1 and 1000.

cursorParam.name: cursor
cursorParam.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous response's `cursor`/`links.next`, used to fetch the next page of a folder listing.

fromParam.name: from
fromParam.description: Indicates the starting date to get logs from. If not specified, uses the current date minus 15 minutes.

toParam.name: to
toParam.description: Indicates the ending date to get logs from. If not specified, uses the current date.

sinceParam.name: since
sinceParam.description: Indicates the time span to retrieve logs for, as a number and a unit in short notation (`s`, `m`, `h` or `d`). Not usable in combination with either `from` or `to`.

nextTokenParam.name: nextToken
nextTokenParam.description: Token returned from a previous call to continue

statusEditUrlParam.name: editUrl
statusEditUrlParam.description: Optional URL of the edit (authoring) document
